rows.why_long: Underdog higher 4.5 needs 56% per pick for your entry; fair view 66% (fanduel 5.5, moved to this line). Averaging 5.3 over the last 8 games, higher than 4.5 in 53% of them (raw 54%, shrunk 65%). Projects 4.9 (raw 50%, shrunk 64%).
why_points: The pick: Receptions higher 4.5 on Underdog. Each pick has to win 56% of the time for a typical entry to make money; the sportsbooks' fair view (fanduel 5.5, moved to this line) is 66%.
Other apps: PrizePicks 6. This is the best number for the higher side.
Game log, most recent first: 4, 4, 7, 5, 9, 6, 3, 5. Weighted average 5.3; went higher than 4.5 in 5 of 8 games (53% recency-weighted).
How much he swings: game to game he typically moves about ±1.7, so the line is 0.4 of those swings below his average (standard deviations) — a modest gap.
PFF unit matchup, for context (in the 2023-25 test it added nothing to the projection, so it is not in the numbers): +18% on his average.
PFF: MIA plays man on 22% of coverage snaps (his opponents so far 24%); he gains 1.14 yds/route vs man and 1.50 vs zone → +1% from scheme.
PFF: MIA allows 1.61 yds/route to TEs after adjusting for the offenses it faced (league 1.45) → +14% against his usual opponents.
Projection: we expect 4.9 catches on average; in a typical game 4.3 (a few big games pull the average up, so the typical game is what we compare with the line) — 0.2 below the line.

Keeping it honest: on their own, recent games (form) say 54% and the matchup 50%. The sportsbooks are usually close to right, and these methods have only partly beaten them (weights measured on NFL week 2), so we pull them most of the way toward the market: form 65%, matchup 64%.
Bottom line: we give it 64% to win and it needs 56%. The edge is the difference: +8.4 points; that works out to about +15¢ per $1 bet over the long run.
